_provenance: Fictional demo data. Household, utility, and account identifiers are invented for the Pax 'Home Energy Guardian' hackathon scenario. No real person, address, or utility account is represented.

baseline.methodology: Weather- and trend-normalized expected usage and bill for this billing period, computed from the same calendar period one year prior (August 2025: 1080 kWh, see usage-history.json) adjusted slightly downward for trend, then billed under the CURRENT tariff (tariff-standard-2026) so the rate change is isolated as a separate factor rather than folded into the baseline. 13.75 + 0.150 * 1075 = 175.00.
baseline.computedBy: bill-normalizer skill (fixture-authored reference value for deterministic tests)

anomaly.arithmeticNote: currentAmount 248.50 / baseline amount 175.00 = 1.42 exactly -> 42% above the normalized baseline. (248.50 - 175.00) = 73.50 dollars above baseline; 73.50 / 175.00 = 0.42.
anomaly.usageGapArithmeticNote: 1565 - 1075 = 490 kWh above the normalized baseline usage. Of this gap, 210 kWh is explained by weather (see weather-history.json) and the remaining 280 kWh is unexplained by rate or weather alone (see household-events.json for the supported thermostat-malfunction hypothesis).
